problem: Memory and control in embodied systems are usually modeled with separate frameworks, which makes them hard to unify and generalize. Prior approaches also typically need task-specific training.
motivation: Embodied agents need both egocentric memory and control to explore unknown environments and answer questions about them. A large language model that communicates with perception modules in natural language could serve as a single zero-shot 'brain' for both.
key_idea: Use an embodied LLM as a robotic brain that keeps egocentric memory and issues control commands, in closed-loop natural-language dialogue with multimodal models for perception and planning, zero-shot.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract suggests that natural language can serve as a common interface for perception, planning, control and memory, so an LLM can handle memory and control together without training.
method: LLM-Brain framework: integrates multiple multimodal language models for robotic tasks in a zero-shot manner
Natural-language communication: all components exchange information via closed-loop multi-round dialogues covering perception, planning, control and memory
Embodied LLM core: maintains egocentric memory and controls the robot
Downstream tasks: active exploration within a limited action budget, and embodied question answering from observations gathered in earlier exploration
